review_notes: I read the whole file. I looked for definitions that compete with Mathlib concepts. The only new definition is `gε`, an abbrev for the functorial map `DualNumber A →ₐ[R] DualNumber B` induced by `g : A →ₐ[R] B`. It is built directly from Mathlib's `DualNumber.lift`. I searched Mathlib's `DualNumber.lean` and `TrivSqZeroExt/Basic.lean`. `TrivSqZeroExt.map` (line 1072) only changes the module, with the base ring fixed. I found no Mathlib `DualNumber.map` or ring-changing map for `TrivSqZeroExt`. So `gε` does not compete with an existing Mathlib declaration. The other declarations are lemmas (`gε_eps`, `gε_comp_toAlgHom`, `stageHom_postComp`, `hom_comm`, `appLE_congr`, `map01_oneAddEpsMul`, `solution`). The rubric excludes standalone theorem duplication, so I did not report any of them. The repo does define similar maps in several files: `liftHom` in two P2M/Sol files, and `dualMap` and `scale` elsewhere. That is repo-internal duplication, not a competing version of a Mathlib concept, and it is outside this file. The `DualNumber.lift ⟨…⟩` expression is also repeated inline in the statement of `solution` instead of using `gε`. That is a style point and not a Mathlib duplicate. The main uncertainty is that I did not search all of Mathlib for an unnamed ring-changing `TrivSqZeroExt` functoriality lemma.
